plugin-data.name: Contact Email
plugin-data.description: Publishes a contact address behind a click. The address is never in the served HTML -- it is encoded, split across randomly-named attributes and only reassembled when a visitor actually clicks.

contact-email-address-tip: Stored in plain text on the server, but never sent to the browser in readable form.
contact-email-link-text-tip: What the visitor clicks. Leave empty for the default.
contact-email-subject-tip: Pre-filled in the visitor's mail client. Leave empty for none.
contact-email-css-class-tip: Added to the button, for theming. The plugin's own class stays regardless.
contact-email-display-tip: The button style adds the theme's own btn classes, so it matches the other buttons on your site. The plugin's fallback styling has zero specificity and never fights the theme.
contact-email-pow-tip: Encrypts the address and makes the browser compute the key before it can be shown. Not a delay a script can skip: without the computation there is no key. A visitor waits a few seconds once; a harvester pays the same for every address on every page load.
contact-email-pow-bits-tip: Each extra bit doubles the work. Measured on a desktop at roughly 650,000 hashes per second: 19 bits is well under half a second, 22 bits about 3 seconds on average (6 at worst), 24 bits about 13 seconds, 26 bits about 50 seconds. A phone is around four times slower. Between 8 and 26; above 24 you are asking a visitor to wait longer than most of them will.
contact-email-debug-tip: Writes a step-by-step account of the reveal to the browser console, and publishes a checksum of the address plus the decryption key alongside it, so the console can say definitively where a decode went wrong. Switch it off again afterwards: while it is on, the key is in the page and the proof of work protects nothing.
contact-email-debug-warning: Debug mode publishes the decryption key in the page, which defeats the proof of work. Switch it on to diagnose a problem, then switch it off again.
contact-email-token-help: Write this anywhere in a page or post to place the button:
contact-email-sidebar-tip: Shows the same button in the theme sidebar, on every page. Requires a theme that renders the siteSidebar hook.
contact-email-failed: The address could not be shown.
contact-email-noscript: JavaScript is required to show the email address.
